messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: DNS resolver latency spike detected in eu-west-1 affecting inference-api-prod. P95 resolver latency > 500ms, backend 5xx rate +8% in last 5m. Alert severity: P2.

pagerduty: @alice (oncall) paging — please acknowledge (rule: geo-dns-resolver-eu).

alice (oncall): acked — looking. grabbing console.

alice (oncall): seeing spike in DNS lookup latencies from our edge-proxies -> upstream resolvers (cloudflare). curl to /v1/generate timed out during name resolution.

ben: I can run dig from a few edge VMs. hold on.

ben: dig +stats @1.1.1.1 inference-api.redwood-inference.internal A
;; Query time: 512 msec
;; SERVER: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)

carla: support dashboard shows a bunch of 502/504s for EU customers starting ~12:07 UTC. no obvious CPU/GPU issues.

dave: looks like our DNS requests are getting slow at resolver layer. Could be Cloudflare edge resolver overload or intermittent Route53 propagation loops.

alice (oncall): quick mitigation idea: switch geoDNS routing policy to fallback pool (route53 weight -> fallback resolvers) to avoid the problematic resolver pool. Need netops sign-off to change resolver chain.

ben: I propose switching edge resolver order to prefer AWS resolver (169.254.169.253 / VPC) for eu-west-1 as short-term. TTLs are low on our internal names but external resolvers cache behavior is noisy.

frank (sre): agree with fallback. Also enable local stub resolver cache increase to 30s and hold open connections longer to reduce immediate churn.

erin (support): heads-up — two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp & VeloHealth) reported degraded API. Customer-facing comms?

alice (oncall): I'll draft a short status message for support to send. ETA 20m for mitigation check.

netops-bot: Proposed change: Update /etc/resolv.conf order on edge-proxies to: 1) aws-vpc-resolver, 2) cloudflare, 3) google. Rolling change to 10% hosts now.

ben: rolling at 10% -> watch metrics.

alice (oncall): command I'm running on one edge node:
```
sudo sed -i '1i nameserver 169.254.169.253' /etc/resolv.conf && systemd-resolve --flush-caches
curl -v https://inference-api.redwood-inference.internal/health || true
```

ben: node test result: curl health now 25ms (was 600ms). Nice.

carla: infra dashboards show incoming 5xx rate dropping from 8% -> 2% for nodes in rollout group. Good signal.

alice (oncall): scaling rollout to 50% across eu-west-1. Monitoring for any regression.

dave: triggered Route53 failover plan to move weighted record to fallback geo-pool (weight 90 -> 10) temporarily. Note: DNS TTL is 30s so full propagation ~30-60s depending on caches.

erin (support): sent initial customer note to impacted accounts: "We've detected degraded API requests in EU due to external DNS resolver latency. We're routing traffic through alternate resolvers and expect recovery within minutes. We'll update in 30 mins."

frank (sre): creating temporary mitigations checklist in incident doc. Add item: enable resolver health checks and alert if QueryTime > 200ms.

alice (oncall): update — metrics stable, 5xx down to 1.1%, latency for DNS lookups p95 < 80ms for rolled hosts. Rolling remainder to 100%.

netops-bot: Completed change: resolv.conf order updated on 100% of edge-proxies in eu-west-1.

ben: still seeing occasional spikes from Cloudflare resolver clients outside VPC. Might be upstream CDN -> resolver path.

dave: follow-on: add route53 health-check to automate failover away from cloudflare resolvers if probe latency > 250ms for 2 consecutive checks.

carla: support: received confirmation from AcmeCorp that API is back to normal. VeloHealth also confirmed.

alice (oncall): assigning post-incident actions: @ben to add resolver health-checks; @dave to add automatic geo-dns fallback policy; @frank to write postmortem; @carla to coordinate customer follow-up.

frank (sre): taking notes for postmortem now — timeline, impact, mitigation, and RCA hypotheses (cloudflare resolver overload + noisy cache invalidation).

alice (oncall): incident status -> mitigated, impact reduced to background levels. Keeping channel open for 60m for monitoring.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged resolved by alice (oncall) at 12:45 UTC.

alice (oncall): small follow-up: add an automated runbook step for future: if resolver P95 > 300ms -> rollback to aws-vpc-resolver order and trigger PD run.

ben: creating ticket: INF-4532 "GeoDNS resiliency: automated resolver failover + health checks"

erin (support): filing customer follow-up drafts now.

frank (sre): postmortem assigned. Will request infra logs and dig traces from Cloudflare for cross-check.

alice (oncall): thanks all. closing handoff in 60m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
